what_happened: The dispatch description states task 298 (the books context corpus tree) 'has not yet run', used as the basis for an ownership-boundary note restricting this task to ADD two new files without restructuring the tree. Checking specs/state.json live shows task 298 has status completed (17 files already landed under agent-system/extensions/books/context/project/books/), and the other three named dependencies (329 issue log, 330 dispatch metrics, 331 observer seam) are also completed. The ownership-boundary intent (add two files, don't restructure) is unaffected and remains correct, but the plan/implementation stage should know the corpus tree already exists with established index-entries.json tiering conventions (README.md is eagerly loaded for the four books agents + task_type books; all 16 other documents are on_demand:true with empty load_when) to mirror when registering the two new files, rather than assuming an empty tree.

The consuming repository had already designed the exact OBSERVATION record this phase froze (seven-dimension vocabulary, polarity enum, repo-side/agent-side field split), discovered during research and confirmed again while writing the standard. Conforming verbatim rather than re-deriving a schema saved a full design pass.

Phase 1/2's tags shape (dimension+polarity only) had no field distinguishing a general negative signal from one half of a paired-burden trade. Discovered while designing Phase 3's read contract. Fixed inline by adding optional tags.burden (created|lifted) and tags.convention_decision sub-fields to both already-committed documents before writing the observer.

books-observe.sh's fail-soft design (jq-optional reads, present-or-absent probe-dependent groups, omit-never-zero) smoke-tested clean on the first pass against four fixture cases (join, empty, malformed issues.jsonl, unresolvable task_dir) -- no retries needed.

Phase 3's standard specified the per-group source:collected|backfilled marker (D2) but the Phase 3 script implementation did not yet attach it anywhere. Discovered while implementing Phase 4's --backfill mode, which needed a concrete place to set source:backfilled. Fixed by refactoring Phase 3's inline body into a shared observe_run_core() function parameterized by is_backfill, and amending observation-record.md's schema to wrap book_requires_churn/validated_by_promotions/verification_tiers/certifier_outcomes/snapshot_delta accordingly.

books-observe.sh's book_requires-churn grep used '^\+[^+].*book_requires', which unconditionally consumes the character right after the leading + via [^+] and then searches the REMAINDER for the literal 'book_requires' -- so a genuinely added line '+book_requires Foo' never matched, because the consumed 'b' broke the literal match. Caught immediately by the test suite's case (1) assertion. Fixed to '^\+[^+]*book_requires' (star, not a single required char), which still correctly excludes '+++'/'---' diff-header lines. A second, independent jq bug in the same build used '[$dims[]] | index(.)' inside a pipe where '.' had already been rebound to the piped array itself, so index() always found the array inside itself (index 0) instead of searching for the dimension value -- fixed by binding the value to a named variable () before the select(), per jq's own index()-argument-evaluation-context semantics.
